prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer sits in a salon chair with their knees, left hand holding a fan of nail swatches on the lower left, and right forearm resting on a towel-draped armrest in the center-right all in bright white-grey at roughly 0.3 to 0.7 metres. To the right of the armrest, a technician leans forward from roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metres away, with her right hand reaching onto the armrest to touch the wearer's right hand (frames 1–4) before lifting up in frame 5 as her head and shoulders rise closer to the camera (bright white on the upper right of frames 4–5). Beyond the wearer's feet, two footrests with footbaths and two small round stools on the wooden floor recede into dark grey and black at roughly 1.2 to 2.0 metres below and in front of the wearer. Compared to the RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the elevated planes of the wearer's lap, swatch fan, armrest, and technician's head from the lower floor and footbaths, even where the technician's black shirt blends into dark surroundings. However, the depth map is unreliable around the thin plastic sticks of the swatch fan—which merge into a solid bright blob—and along the right frame edge where the technician's hair and face saturate into an indistinct white patch.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates a single large pink 'person' mask on the right half of all five frames, combining the leaning technician (~0.6–1.0 metres away, partly cut off by the right frame edge) with the camera wearer's own right forearm and hand resting on the central armrest (~0.5 metres away) whenever they are in contact. Because both arms are within immediate reach and touching in frames 1–4, the mask merges the technician's reaching right arm and torso with the wearer's right hand into one connected region, while the gap between the technician's left and right arms forms a black cutout underneath her torso. Across the sequence, as the technician releases the wearer's hand and sits upright in frame 5, the pink mask shifts upward and right, though the wearer's right arm remains erroneously attached to the bottom of her mask and mislabelled as a purple 'banana'. While the map highlights the combined occupancy of the interacting arms on the right, it is highly unreliable elsewhere: it completely misses the camera wearer's legs and left hand on the left, hallucinating a 'cup' on a floor stool in frame 1 and labelling the yellow nail file (frame 4) and the wearer's right forearm (frame 5) as 'banana'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the upper-body skeleton (yellow) and right-hand joints (magenta) of the technician on the right side of the scene, located roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metres from the camera wearer. In frames 1–4, her torso and shoulder links angle downward and to the right, showing her leaning deeply forward with her head near the right edge facing down toward the armrest and away from the camera wearer's face. Her right arm extends left into the centre of the frame—within arm's reach of both people—where the detailed magenta hand skeleton overlaps the wearer's right hand in frames 1–4, while her left arm extends downward toward the wearer's right foot in frames 1–3 before dropping out of tracking in frame 4. In frame 5, as the technician lifts her torso and brings both hands together above the armrest, the entire yellow body skeleton fails to detect, leaving only a cluster of magenta hand keypoints where her two hands meet. This map makes the technician's hunched torso geometry, shoulder orientation, and fine finger articulation much clearer than in the dark-clothed RGB view, but it is unreliable in missing the camera wearer's own body and hands entirely and losing the technician's body pose in frame 5.
